newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends sharply higher on stocks, stops.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends sharply higher on stocks, stops.

text.p: COMEX copper futures ended sharply higher Tuesday, in line with LME copper, helped by a further large draw in LME warehouse copper stocks and by the execution of stop orders above key resistance levels.

"LME copper stocks are getting down near 10-year lows, tightening up the prompt market and forcing a breach of resistance above 90 cents in COMEX December copper which triggered some stop orders," Refco's New York analyst James Steel said.
COMEX December copper ened up 3.20 cents at 91.65 cents, after seeing a 10-day high at 91.70 cents intraday.

December copper has traded around 90 cents for three months, swinging in a side range between 85 cents and 95 cents, which has meant 90 cents has become something of a pivot point for short term traders, analysts said.
The December/March backwardation ended wider, around 1.50 cents, after narrowing from 2.30 cents on August 30 to 0.50 cent on September 20, as prompt supply tightened.
LME copper warehouse stocks fell 8,625 tonnes to 220,950 tonnes Tuesday, while COMEX copper stocks fell 845 short tons Monday to 19,720 short tons.

But Bloomsbury Mineral Economics in London calculates there will probably be a global copper supply surplus of around 175,000 tonnes in the second half of 1996, while in 1997 the surplus could rise to 250,000-300,000 tonnes, analysts noted.
